sources.title: Makivvik and Nunavik partners, Parnasimautik Consultation Report
sources.note: Community consultation report page 3 describes Nunavik geography, Inuit homeland, archaeology, seasonal life, foods, early European contact, and later colonial change.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, The Region of Nunavik
sources.note: Nunavik Inuit cultural institution explains the living place-name, regional scale, long occupation, Inuit arrival, later change, and Taamusi Qumaq place-name testimony.

sources.title: Makivvik Land Administration System, Region
sources.note: Nunavik Inuit organization distinguishes modern mainland and marine regions, 14 coastal villages, Chisasibi, shared-use areas, and current legal geography.

sources.title: Nunavik Parks, Our Culture
sources.note: Nunavik institution summarizes archaeology, seasonal family groups, foods, material technologies, katajjaniq, carving, and historically dated later changes.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Nunavik Land Lexicon
sources.note: Community lexicon defines clothing, baby-carrying amautik, tools, dwelling types, transport, lamp, and natsiq as ringed seal.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Our Tools
sources.note: Community tool guide describes qajaq, umiaq, kakivak, unaaq, qulliq, ulu, skin work, materials, and task specialization.

sources.title: Taamusi Qumaq, All That Is Precious to Us
sources.note: A dated 1992 Nunavik elder account of rivers, fish, drinking water, snow, seasonal shelters, dogs, travel, materials, descendants, and continuity.

sources.title: Avataq Puurtaq Project, Inuit Have Always Been Busy
sources.note: Community memory project describes hunting, sewing, children helping parents and grandparents, snow clearing, hide work, driftwood, lamps, and autumn cold.

sources.title: Avataq Puurtaq Project, Making Qajaqs
sources.note: Community memory project describes driftwood selection, named frame pieces, sealskin preparation, specialized sewing, shared labor, celebration, portage, and family travel.

sources.title: Avataq Puurtaq Project, Life in an Igloo
sources.note: Community memory project records family-sized snow houses, cleaning, light, bedding, urine, water and waste chores, elders, lamps, cold, and lice.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Traditional Medicine
sources.note: Report based on 1983 elder group interviews in all 14 communities, emphasizing shared but variable knowledge, specialists, experimentation, and historical change.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Pregnancy and Birth
sources.note: Community traditional-medicine archive records midwifery knowledge and birth care from later elder interviews; used descriptively, never as medical advice.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, The Passing On of Traditional Stories and Tales in Nunavik
sources.note: Two-page historical summary covers oral teaching, audience correction, regional dialects, late introduction of writing, syllabics, and Mitiarjuk Nappaaluk.

sources.title: Kativik Ilisarniliriniq Nunavik-IcE, Standard Orthography
sources.note: Official Nunavik education resource gives paired alphabetic and syllabic forms, exact examples, consonant rules, nineteenth-century history, and the 1976 standard.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Inuktitut Language Department
sources.note: Nunavik Inuit institution documents the 1984 elders language commission, Taamusi Qumaq dictionary, terminology work, publications, and living language stewardship.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Genealogy Methodology
sources.note: Community genealogy guide explains Inukjuak interviews, family verification, customary adoption, kin terms, and sauniq namesake relationships.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Archaeology Department History
sources.note: Community institutional history describes Daniel Weetaluktuk, the 1983 elders resolution, department mandate, youth fieldwork, collaboration, and recorded sites.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Nunaingok (Ikirasaq) Site
sources.note: Community archaeology page documents mixed-period structures, qarmait, sleeping platform and entrance, long chronology, thousands of artifacts, and Inuit student training.

sources.title: Barbel et al., Paaliup Qarmangit 1 Site Geoarchaeology
sources.note: Peer-reviewed abstract identifies a single-family winter Thule-Inuit house, calibrated occupation ranges bracketing 1492, resource choices, and post-depositional mixing.

sources.title: Bhiry, Marguerie, and Lofthouse, Paleoenvironmental Reconstruction at Quaqtaq
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study separates Dorset and Thule Inuit occupations, reconstructs fall and winter marine-mammal use, environmental phases, and revised dating.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Place Names
sources.note: Community project records an elders mandate to collect, confirm, map, publish, and encourage everyday use of Inuit place names.

sources.title: Martin et al., Drinking Water and Potential Threats to Human Health in Nunavik
sources.note: Peer-reviewed 2003 to 2004 study distinguishes source water from household containers and recommends monitoring and improved modern water and wastewater systems.

sources.title: Nunavik Parks, Frequently Asked Questions
sources.note: Current official visitor guidance covers hydration, treating water, cat-hole dimensions and distances, packing out paper, washing, waste, and artifact protection.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Archival Centre
sources.note: Community archive inventories oral histories, photographs, drawings, medicine interviews, Puurtaq memories, and twentieth-century change with collection dates.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Home
sources.note: Nunavik Inuit cultural institution presents living language, culture, heritage work, elders, youth, collections, and continuing community stewardship.

sources.title: Kativik School Board, Through Mala’s Eyes
sources.note: Nunavik education resource dates contact and settlement changes, describes current sharing and schooling, and identifies Inuktitut as the dominant regional language.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Airport Archaeological Pre-assessment
sources.note: Community-led 1985 to 1987 inventories around nine communities identified more than 250 sites, excavated four, and protected threatened cultural remains.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Collections
sources.note: Community institution describes archaeology, documentary, art, and ethnography collections and their evidence for long regional presence, daily life, ingenuity, and expression.

sources.title: Taamusi Qumaq, Kangirsuk
sources.note: Dated 1992 community portrait explains Arctic char variation, ice fishing with kakivak, tides, hospitality, travel, and living Inuktitut.

sources.title: Avataq Cultural Institute, Archaeology Department
sources.note: Elders-mandated department identifies, studies, protects, and preserves Nunavik archaeological heritage while involving communities, elders, and youth.
